title: An instruction is not a guard
statement: Telling an agent not to change content doesn't stop it: hash content files before and after automated work, and keep every change as an edit that can be replayed.
example: An agent told never to edit a lesson file overwrote it from a stale copy, caught only because a test's count came out 186 instead of 187.
detail: During a fan-out of model agents in the reading project, one agent left the lesson file at a stale snapshot and four content edits vanished, despite an explicit prompt clause never to edit that file; it was caught only because a test's count pin came out 186 instead of 187 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd`). The root cause it records is that a prompt instruction is not a write guard, since an agent's shell can write wherever the main loop can; the fix is to hash every content file before a fan-out, check it when each agent returns, treat any change as an incident, and keep every content change as an operations file so re-applying it is one command (the same file).

evidence.quote: left the working file at a 21:15 snapshot — four content ops (tappability spans, a decoy line) vanished — despite an explicit prompt clause "never edit public/lesson-json/grade-3.json." Caught only because `semantic-coverage.test.mjs`'s count pin moved (186 ≠ 187).
**Root cause:** a prompt instruction is not a write guard — a fan-out's Bash has the same filesystem

before any fan-out that touches harnesses/tests, record `md5 -q public/lesson-json/grade-3.json` (and any other content file); re-check it when every agent returns and treat any change as an incident (re-apply from saved ops files, never hand-patch). Keep every content mutation as an ops file under the batch record (`apply-ops.py`) so re-application is one idempotent command.
I compared the entire current U9 Lesson7 parsed object with baseline da0b0b42 after excluding only that new node. **They are equal.**
Lesson for the fan-out rule: forbid any JSON write in the prompt AND check the file's md5 after agents return.
only 1 of 4 authored options survived; that is a rewrite, not a form edit
--check  rebuilds in memory and fails if the committed JSON differs or any quote is not verbatim.
